# Original Object257 first atom: source candidate

This candidate contains one new actual leaf certificate and one concrete
production fold-state theorem. **All three native phases are NOT_RUN.** The
source preparation and structural audit are not compiler admission, a proof,
Object component acceptance, or production PrismPM acceptance.

The leaf certificate retains the original `objTrace257Record0` statement for
bytes 0 through 31 and asks Reflexivity to compute its actual identity. Its old
Hash/Wrapper helper theorems are not imported. The expected record ID remains
`[63,164,31,162,68,35,68,195,38,116,35,81]`.

The Prop family reuses the unchanged accepted `Obj257TerminalContext` and the
supported Nat Induction/Cases/Congruence proof shape. The consumer is the actual
production call `ObjFoldAtoms [[0,1,...,31]] [] [] originalLimits`, with the
retained concrete singleton inventory and frontier as its expected result.
Apply at 1 must establish the production conversion and concrete state. The
source does not assume that this conversion succeeds.

The negative source was authored first. It differs from the positive semantic
module only in the expected consumer inventory record ID's first byte, 63 to 64.
Its expected frontier, leaf certificate, family and lifted proof remain unchanged.
An import, certificate, parser, timeout or resource failure is not the intended
negative result.

## Portable staging and native phases

`candidate.json` lists every shared input as a repository-relative `path`, its
SHA-256, and a stage-relative `destination`. The shared inputs are the ten exact
runtime modules, unchanged terminal context, and three Lean workspace files in
`../object257-leaf-transport/project/`. No runtime closure is duplicated here.
The four new modules have equivalent mappings in `newStageInputs`. Verify these
identities before staging. Keep the existing project files and original drafts
unchanged; use an independently owned stage or restore a reused diagnostic stage
under its existing custody rules.

For each phase, select the corresponding `phases/<phase>/lexlean.toml` as the
stage's `lexlean.toml`. The configs differ from the accepted terminal config only
in their entrypoint. They retain the 300,000 ms child limit and original source,
language and Lean settings. Generate and retain a genuine development lock with
the installed official compiler; this candidate supplies no fabricated lock.
The parent owns exact compiler/container/resource checks and the ordinary lock
command used for prior phases. Run the following from the fully prepared stage:

| Phase | Root | Source check | Verification |

| `leaf-positive` | `tests/lexlean/Object257FirstAtomLeaf.lex.tex` | `lexlean --diagnostic-format json check tests/lexlean/Object257FirstAtomLeaf.lex.tex` | `lexlean --diagnostic-format json verify tests/lexlean/Object257FirstAtomLeaf.lex.tex` |
| `state-false` | `tests/lexlean/Object257FirstAtomStateFalseId.lex.tex` | `lexlean --diagnostic-format json check tests/lexlean/Object257FirstAtomStateFalseId.lex.tex` | `lexlean --diagnostic-format json verify tests/lexlean/Object257FirstAtomStateFalseId.lex.tex` |
| `state-positive` | `tests/lexlean/Object257FirstAtomState.lex.tex` | `lexlean --diagnostic-format json check tests/lexlean/Object257FirstAtomState.lex.tex` | `lexlean --diagnostic-format json verify tests/lexlean/Object257FirstAtomState.lex.tex` |

After internal source review, first isolate the actual leaf certificate, then
require the source-valid state negative to fail at the wrong consumer result,
then verify the positive. Preserve all actual command receipts and resource
failures. No automatic larger-memory or equivalent retry is implied. Audit the

The original 257-byte fold digest, eight later atoms, full continuation bridge,
